title: bitcircus101 jobs.json
description: Job board behind pinnwand.html: one object per posting, each a LINK to a vacancy hosted elsewhere. Holds no applicant data, no contact details and no amounts — the donation is handled outside this file.

postings.description: Every posting ever paid for that is still up. Remove an entry once check-jobs.mjs warns that it expired. Two rules this schema cannot express, which scripts/check-jobs.mjs enforces on top: ids must be unique across the array, and company/title must hold at least one non-blank character.

chiffre.description: Anonymous notes from people looking for work ("unter Chiffre"). No name, no contact details: companies write to info@bitcircus101.de with the subject CHIFFRE <id>, and the space forwards the mail to an address that is never in this repo. Optional: a board without the key shows the empty Chiffre slot alone.

karussell.description: The permanent slot (Dauerplatz): the last card on the wall cycles through these entries, one name and one https link each. No dates — a slot is booked per year and the list is curated by hand; remove an entry when its year runs out. Optional: a board without the key shows the invite note alone.

id.description: Slug used in DOM ids and URLs — lowercase, digits, dashes. Convention: <company>-<yyyy>-<mm>.

company.description: Who is hiring, as it should appear on the card.

title.description: The vacancy, in one line. Where it is goes into `location`.

location.description: Where the work happens: a city, a region, remote — or all of it, e.g. "Bonn oder remote".

employment.description: What kind of work it is, one or more of: full-time, part-time, working-student, internship, apprenticeship, freelance. The card shows the German label.

url.description: Link to the vacancy — https only; we host nothing, we link.

from.description: First day the posting is shown (YYYY-MM-DD). It runs until the day before the same day-of-month `months` later.

months.description: How long the note hangs, in months: 1, 3 or 12 — nothing else. No amount belongs anywhere near it: a note goes up because somebody asked, not because they paid, and neither this file nor the page's own copy names a currency (a posting's title is the company's text and may say what it likes).

id.description: The Chiffre number, handed out by the space: 0x plus two to four lowercase hex digits. It is the mail subject (CHIFFRE 0x2a), so it must be unique.

headline.description: What the person does and looks for, in one line — no name, no current employer.

level.description: Experience in three coarse bands: entry, experienced, senior.

skills.description: One to eight lowercase tags, e.g. rust, kicad, c++.

about.description: A few sentences, no contact details — those come in the forwarded mail.

name.description: The company, as it should appear on the card. Capped at 24 characters so the name fits the card's one-line title on a phone: the title swaps every few seconds and must never change height.

url.description: Where the name links — https only; we host nothing, we link.
